posts.cooked:
Silverleaf:

Why is a remake a good thing? Doesn't the original still exist? Genuinely confused here.

Hardware limitations have changed drastically over the years, and it's kind of cool to see what the game could look like run on a new gen console. It's basically like restoring a work of art or making a new edition of a book. The question of whether or not how good it is will be dependent on how much is changed, but at the same time, I would at least like to see FF7's story and aesthetics attempted with modern hardware and the ability to have voice acting to both tell the story and better define the characters…

phantaskippy wrote:

Great game, but now it is really dated.  Not just graphics either, the gameolay doesn't hold up.  
How does the gameplay not hold up? The basic mechanics of the game were pretty solid, and the materia system is still a great way to customize characters even in today's market. The mechanics of most classic videogames like Mario and Chrono Trigger I would say still hold their own in the modern world, which is why people still play these games.



The problem is that Final Fantasy VII was a very graphics-driven game; it primarily sold off the FMV cutscenes, which at the time were quite rare in console games. Any graphics-driven game tends to become rather underwhelming as time goes on. Now if you go back and play V which was driven by gameplay or VI which was driven by the story, then you can still enjoy them greatly even if you have no nostalgic attachment to it, but VII was ultimately forgettable for anyone that didn't grow up during that era.
